title: Integration discovery - Avalon Systems
summary: Discovery focused on integration patterns for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy strategy for rate limiting and caching, observability hooks (tracing, logs), and security requirements (SSO, KMS, audit logs). Customer wants guidance on latency/cost tradeoffs and a POC for their search/assist use case.
topics: Gateway/proxy vs direct SDK calls (cached prefix, request routing)
Rate limits, quotas and burst handling
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (VPC, KMS, data retention)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll run about 45 minutes, 50 minutes. quick intros - I'm Jordan from Redwood, Leah is our systems engineer.
[00:12] Rajesh Patel: Hey thanks, Rajesh here, CTO at Avalon. we mainly care about latency for our realtime search assist and security requirements.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Maya - I manage the eng team building the assist product. we use LangChain and a bit of LlamaIndex for our retrieval pipeline.
[00:27] Jordan Park: great, that's exactly the integration topic. Leah - do you want to cover SDK and LangChain adapters?
[00:31] Leah Martinez: sure, quick overview: Redwood offers first-class SDKs in python/js and we have out-of-the-box connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex, so you can swap the backend to Redwood with minimal code. sometimes the connector names are slightly off in doc auto, but we have examples.
[00:46] Toni Ruiz: are those connectors officially supported? we rely on the LangChain chain of chains thing, so compatibility matters.
[00:52] Leah Martinez: yes supported; we maintain adapter examples for LangChain's chains, and for LlamaIndex we have templates for vector store integration - and we also give sample batching/caching config. there are small edge cases around streaming and function calling but we provide pattern docs.
[01:09] Maya Chen: streaming is big for us - user sees tokens as they type. how does streaming work with dedicated/private?
[01:15] Leah Martinez: streaming works across Hosted, Dedicated and Private. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower tail latency because of reserved GPU pools; Private (VPC) has the same API surface but runs in your VPC - slightly more network overhead depending on peering.
[01:28] Rajesh Patel: network overhead - do you have numbers? we're worried about 95th percentile for a 1k token context.
[01:35] Leah Martinez: ballpark: Hosted median generation latency for similar models is demo reference - for Dedicated you typically see 10-30% improvement in P95 under reserved capacity. we'll send detailed perf notes but it depends on model, sequence length, and batching.
[01:51] Oliver Grant: security: we need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS integration and audit logs. can you run in our VPC and use our KMS?
[01:58] Jordan Park: yes - Private deployment supports customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM options, we also support SAML SSO and RBAC. Audit logs and request-level retention settings are configurable for Dedicated/Private. Hosted can support DPA and longer retention with enterprise plans.
[02:14] Oliver Grant: fine - for compliance we need proof. can you share SOC2 and network architecture?
[02:19] Jordan Park: absolutely, we'll send our security pack (SOC2 report, data flow diagrams, encryption at rest and in transit details).
[02:26] Maya Chen: on the integration side we have an internal gateway that applies user quotas and does some caching. we'd prefer not to double proxy. what's your recommended pattern - call Redwood directly from service or route through our gateway?
[02:37] Leah Martinez: two common patterns: 1) direct SDK from app to Redwood with per-route API keys and our built-in quotas and rate limits; 2) use a customer-side gateway/proxy for additional caching, business rules, and auth. If you already have a gateway, the typical setup is to keep your gateway as the single egress point and set Redwood to trust that IP or use a mutual TLS setup for Private/Dedicated. For Hosted, we support IP allowlists and token scoping.
[03:03] Toni Ruiz: sounds good. If we keep our gateway, can we still use Redwood's token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards?
[03:09] Jordan Park: yes, you can emit request IDs from your gateway and pass them in the X-Request-ID header. our tracing and audit logs will surface those IDs - observability hooks integrate with Datadog/OpenTelemetry and we have webhooks for events.
[03:22] Rajesh Patel: about rate limits - we need bursts during peak usage. how do quotas work?
[03:27] Leah Martinez: Hosted has per-account and per-key rate limits with configurable quota windows; Dedicated lets you set throughput policies on the GPU pool - you can do steady baseline plus burst buckets. we also support burst protections and automatic fallback to smaller models if capacity is constrained.
[03:43] Maya Chen: can we do client-side rate limiting plus Redwood serverside? we'd like throttling close to the user.
[03:49] Leah Martinez: yep, common. client-side/backpressure + Redwood's server-side quotas is recommended. caching prefixes / KV cache for repeated prefixes can drastically reduce cost and latency - we'll show examples.
[03:59] Toni Ruiz: observability again - do you expose spans and metrics? we use Datadog and open telem.
[04:05] Jordan Park: we expose metrics (per model/route/token) and traces via OpenTelemetry; for Datadog we have an integration that maps traces and sends metrics - you can also pull logs from the console or via our logs API.
[04:16] Leah Martinez: small note: sometimes the auto transcript in our docs says 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache' - apologies to the transcriber, but you'll see KV cache examples.
[04:23] Maya Chen: okay, on the SDK - how do we handle LangChain agents that expect streaming and tool calls?
[04:30] Leah Martinez: we support function/tool calling and streaming; in LangChain you map the tool calls to our function call responses. we have example agents using the python SDK and conversation state. There are small wrinkles around stop token semantics, but again we have utilities.
[04:47] Rajesh Patel: about embeddings - we rely on vector DBs and want deterministic embeddings for recall. how do you handle versioning and reproducibility?
[04:55] Jordan Park: we provide model version pinning and embedding model aliases; you can pin a model version for the POC; we also surface model performance profiles and change logs in the console.
[05:06] Toni Ruiz: do you provide per-token cost breakdowns for embedding+query pipelines?
[05:11] Jordan Park: yes, console shows token counts, cost by route, and you can instrument sampling to get unit economics.
[05:17] Maya Chen: we will likely start with Hosted to validate, then move to Dedicated for predictability if numbers look good. what's the normal POC flow?
[05:24] Jordan Park: typical flow: 1) trial Hosted credits + sample connectors for LangChain/LlamaIndex, 2) run benchmarks with your workload (we can help run against our test harness), 3) if you like numbers, we propose Dedicated reserved capacity and an SLA, or Private if you need VPC / KMS.
[05:40] Rajesh Patel: timeline - we want a pilot in 4-16 weeks. is that feasible?
[05:45] Leah Martinez: yes, 4-16 weeks is reasonable for an initial POC - we'll scope benchmark tests and provide config examples.
[05:52] Oliver Grant: one more on encryption: for Private, we need to keep keys in our HSM. supported?
[05:58] Jordan Park: yes, HSM/KMS integration is supported for Private and can be arranged for Dedicated via our enterprise plan.
[06:04] Maya Chen: thanks. can you share sample config for LangChain connector and an example gateway pattern?
[06:09] Leah Martinez: absolutely - we'll attach a repo with examples and a sample gateway nginx config and small node/python snippets that show setting X-Request-ID, passing user metadata, and streaming.
[06:21] Rajesh Patel: any blockers from your side to start the pilot?
[06:24] Jordan Park: none - just access to a small dataset and a test account; we'll provide test API keys and a short runbook.
[06:30] Jordan Park: quick recap of next steps and owners - we'll record this, and Leah will follow up with technical artifacts.
[06:36] Maya Chen: cool, thanks everyone.
[06:40] Jordan Park: thanks, we'll follow up in email.
[06:44] (call ends)
